leads.summary: The new heading regression pin still accepts a commented-out noon viewDate; model pins still accept block-commented noon constructors
leads.consequence: If the live Panel.qml viewDate is restored to midnight and the noon declaration is left as a // comment, assertion 140 passes even though the first-of-month heading regression is back. In Model.js, an active midnight constructor with the noon expression left in a block comment also passes the new cursor pin. The new stripping only handles entire // lines in modelSource, and panelSource is not stripped at all. This is a test-strength defect, not evidence the current production code is wrong.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; panelSource part published; block/trailing-comment variant kept private as contrived

leads.summary: Noon is not guaranteed to exist when an entire local date is skipped
leads.consequence: For historical December 2011 in Pacific/Apia, the December 30 grid cell is absent and the week is [26,27,28,29,31,1,2]. This limitation predates the PR's noon fix, but contradicts the new code comment's 'Noon always survives the switch' premise as a general rule. It affects calendars browsed across date-line jumps, not ordinary hour-long DST changes. UTC calendar arithmetic, as proposed in another open PR, avoids needing a local instant for each civil date.
leads.triage: dropped; Apia 2011-12-30 never existed locally; R1 already disclosed date-line days as the only difference from plain calendar arithmetic, identical to base. Not a regression.

leads.summary: Open UTC-grid PR #13186 conflicts with this PR's grid and source-pinned tests
leads.consequence: PR #13186 changes the same leading/cursor and cursor-step lines to UTC, and adds tests in the same September-test insertion point. Combining its intended UTC grid with this PR's unchanged source pins makes pins 137 and 138 fail, even though a UTC grid avoids nonexistent local dates. If both are merged, the overlapping Model.js and clock-test.sh hunks and mutually exclusive pins need manual reconciliation. Open PR #13096 likewise changes the same cursor line and inserts tests at the same place but uses noon, so it duplicates the fix and has a test-hunk merge conflict rather than a UTC-versus-noon behaviour conflict.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13127#issuecomment-5824480412) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13127#issuecomment-5826625569), checked at `3f6fe3d2`.

**Verified:** both points from the earlier review are addressed. One small gap remains: the new heading pin can still be satisfied by a commented-out line.

| Earlier point | Status at `3f6fe3d2` |
|---|---|
| Month heading built from local midnight on the 1st | Resolved |
| `modelSource` pins matched without comment stripping | Resolved for the three `Model.js` pins. The new `Panel.qml` heading pin has the same gap. |

### Month heading: resolved

**Verified:** `Panel.qml:46` now builds `viewDate` at noon. The exact `viewDate` and heading expressions from `Panel.qml` were evaluated in the Qt 6.11.2 QML engine (non-GUI core mode):

| Zone, month | Before (`622aebc4`) | Now (`3f6fe3d2`) |
|---|---|---|
| America/Havana, April 2012 | MARCH 2012 | APRIL 2012 |
| Africa/Cairo, August 2014 | JULY 2014 | AUGUST 2014 |

- A sweep of 341 zones, every month from 1900 through 2100, finds no wrong heading at the new head. The previous expression named the previous month in 487 cases, none after Cairo, August 2014.
- `Qt.formatDate` switches to the UTC date only for an instant in the first second of a UTC day. A noon anchor on the 1st cannot trigger that into another month (at UTC-12 it gives the 2nd of the same month).
- Reverting `viewDate` to midnight makes the new pin fail, in line with the negative control the reply mentions. The clock test passes at head (164 ok) under `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/Santiago`.

### Comment stripping: resolved for `Model.js`, open for the heading pin

**Verified:** `modelSource` is now comment-stripped. For each of the three `Model.js` pins, a copy with that line reverted to midnight and a commented-out noon line above it now fails at that pin. The same copy passes the previous test file.

**Optional test improvement:** the new heading pin (`clock-test.sh:140`) tests `panelSource`, which is read without stripping (`clock-test.sh:14`). A `Panel.qml` with the noon line commented out above an active midnight line passes the full head test (164 ok, exit 0, under both time zones). The reply's "a commented-out constructor cannot satisfy the pins" therefore holds for the `Model.js` pins but not this one. Anchoring the pin to the start of a line closes the gap. With this regex the head test passes, and both the commented-out and the reverted copies fail at the heading pin:

```js
/^\s*readonly property date viewDate: new Date\(viewYear, viewMonth, 1, 12\)/m
```

Stripping comments from `panelSource` also closes it, but `clock-test.sh:237` uses the `// Hairline` comment in `Panel.qml` as the end marker of a source slice. Stripping removes that marker, so that check silently covers the rest of the file (the test still passes).

**Unchanged:** `Model.js` is identical at `622aebc4` and `3f6fe3d2`, so the earlier grid, `stepMonth`, ISO week and today-marking results still apply. `viewDate` has one consumer, the heading. No regressions were found in the changed code.

**Related open PRs:** #12943, #13096 and #13186 change the same `monthGrid` lines for the same DST bug. #12943 and #13096 use the same noon anchor, and #13096 also anchors `viewDate`. #13186 builds the grid in UTC instead. The two conflict in `monthGrid`, and whichever version is kept fails the other's new tests: this PR's pins at `clock-test.sh:137-138`, or #13186's Pacific/Apia 2011 assertion.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit, `Panel.qml`, `clock-test.sh`, and Qt Declarative 6.11.2 `Date` and `Qt.formatDate` code. Runtime checks used the Qt 6.11.2 QML engine in non-GUI core mode to evaluate the heading expressions (targeted cases and the zone sweep, tzdata 2026c), and ran `clock-test.sh` under Node 26.7.0 on the current head, the earlier head, base and mutated copies, with `TZ=UTC` for all and `TZ=America/Santiago` for both heads and most copies. The popup was not rendered on screen and Quickshell was not launched. The related PRs were compared by their diffs and a file-level merge of `Model.js`, not a full merge.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
